title: Multiple-Row Seating Arrangements
tagline: Year 3 — Two or more parallel rows facing each other: facing directions, opposite pairs and mixed left-right clues

introduction.overview: In a multiple-row puzzle people sit in two parallel rows that face each other. The two rows face opposite directions, so the same word "left" points east for one row and west for the other. The key moves are to fix the directions at the start, translate every clue into compass terms, and use "opposite" clues to link the rows seat by seat.
introduction.placementRelevance: Two-row seating sets with eight people and five or six questions are common in written aptitude tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Facing benches in a train compartment, desks in two-sided lab tables and theatre rows are arranged this way.

learningObjectives: Assign facing directions to each row
Convert left and right into east and west
Use opposite pairs to link the rows

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Facing north, left is west and right is east. Facing south, left is east and right is west.

coreDefinitions: Row 1 faces south: left = east, right = west.
Row 2 faces north: left = west, right = east.
Opposite: the person in the same column of the other row.
Extreme end: the first or last seat of a row.
Column: seat number counted from the west in either row.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Two facing rows are a grid with two lines and four columns. Compass directions never change, so translate every left or right into east or west first and then forget about facing.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Draw two rows, mark west and east, note the facing direction of each row, and convert all clues. Place end-of-row and opposite clues first.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Counting
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: East of seat c: 4 − c people

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Check
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Test each clue on the final grid

mainNarrative: Eight friends A to H sit in two rows of four. Row 1 faces south and Row 2 faces north. Take the clues: A is opposite B; C is at the west end of Row 1; F is at the west end of Row 2; H is immediately left of A; E is at the east end of Row 1; D is opposite H; G is immediately right of D. Start with the anchors: C is seat 1 of Row 1 and E is seat 4 of Row 1. F is seat 1 of Row 2, so C and F are opposite.

Row 1 faces south, so the left of A is east. H is immediately east of A. The only free seats in Row 1 are 2 and 3, so A is seat 2 and H is seat 3. B is opposite A, so B is seat 2 of Row 2; D is opposite H, so D is seat 3 of Row 2. Row 2 faces north, so the right of D is east, which is seat 4 of Row 2: G. The row is: Row 1 C, A, H, E and Row 2 F, B, D, G.

The facing directions trap people. In Row 1 "immediately left" means one seat east, and in Row 2 it means one seat west. Writing "east" or "west" beside each clue before placing anyone removes the confusion.
Opposite clues transfer information between rows. If you know someone's column in one row, their opposite has the same column in the other row.
Exchange questions need a fresh copy of the grid. Swap the two names and read the opposite of the person asked about.

deepDiveAspects.title: Diagonal clues
deepDiveAspects.content: A person diagonally opposite to X is in the other row and one column away; check both options if the clue does not say which side.

deepDiveAspects.title: Mixed facing
deepDiveAspects.content: If a puzzle makes both rows face north, the left of everyone is west; read the facing statement carefully.

solvedExamples.title: Direction conversion
solvedExamples.question: Row 1 faces south, with C, A, H, E from west to east. Who is immediately to the left of A?

steps.title: Direction
steps.explanation: Facing south, the left hand points east.

steps.title: Seat
steps.explanation: The seat east of A is occupied by H.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Facing north the answer would be C.

solvedExamples.title: Opposite link
solvedExamples.question: Row 1 is C, A, H, E (west to east) and Row 2 is F, B, D, G. Who sits opposite H?

solvedExamples.title: Counting
solvedExamples.question: In the same arrangement, how many people sit to the east of B in Row 2?

steps.title: Column
steps.explanation: B is seat 2 from the west.

steps.title: East
steps.explanation: Seats 3 and 4 are east of B: 2 people.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Rewrite every left/right as east/west using the row's facing direction, then place anchors.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using one direction for both rows

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: An option that puts two people in one seat is wrong.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Eight-person sets give five or six questions, so build the grid once.

easy.question:
Eight friends A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit in two parallel rows of four seats. Row 1 faces south and Row 2 faces north, so each person in Row 1 faces a person in Row 2. Seats in each row are numbered from west to east. The following facts are known:
1. A sits exactly opposite B.
2. C sits at the western end of Row 1.
3. F sits at the western end of Row 2.
4. H sits immediately to the left of A.
5. E sits at the eastern end of Row 1.
6. D sits exactly opposite H.
7. G sits immediately to the right of D.

Who sits exactly opposite A?
easy.explanation: Row 1 (west to east): C, A, H, E. Row 2 (west to east): F, B, D, G. The person opposite A is B.
